blocks.p: Access to healthcare involves more than identifying a nearby facility. Patients must also determine whether the facility offers an appropriate service, whether a clinician is available, and how to continue care after a consultation. In the Philippines, the 2018 health system review describes regional and socioeconomic differences in access to resources and identifies fragmentation of service delivery as a continuing challenge (Dayrit et al., 2018). These concerns provide a context for examining how information systems can support healthcare navigation and coordination.

When facility information, appointment requests, medical documents, and follow-up communication are handled through separate channels, patients and healthcare personnel must reconcile information across several steps. A request for consultation must be reviewed, a schedule must be confirmed, and supporting documents must reach an authorized clinician. Without a coordinated workflow, users may have difficulty identifying the current status of a request or the next action required. This project addresses that workflow problem within the scope of a mobile and web application.

Digital health offers an opportunity to connect these activities through a shared information system. However, technology alone does not establish an effective service. The World Health Organization’s Global Strategy on Digital Health 2020–2027 emphasizes the need to integrate organizational, human, financial, and technological resources into digital health initiatives (World Health Organization, 2025). For this project, that perspective supports a design that considers the responsibilities of patients, doctors, hospital administrators, and platform administrators, together with the protection of patient information.

This project presents CareNavigator PH, a healthcare navigation and care coordination application for guest and registered users. It seeks to answer the following development question: How can a mobile and web system connect facility discovery, hospital-reviewed booking, consultation tracking, and clinical documentation while preserving clear responsibilities and controlled access? The project evaluates the implemented workflows through software verification. It does not claim to measure changes in health outcomes or population-wide access to care.

To develop a mobile and web application that helps users discover appropriate healthcare facilities and coordinate consultations, clinical records, and care communications through authorized, role-specific workflows.

blocks.p: The project provides a practical model for coordinating healthcare information across user roles. Patients can follow consultation requests and manage supporting documents; doctors can review authorized information and produce structured clinical records; hospital staff can manage appointments and facility operations. For student developers, the system demonstrates how interface design, transactional workflows, and access controls can be combined in a healthcare application. These are intended contributions of the design rather than measured clinical benefits.

blocks.p: CareNavigator PH uses a layered client and managed-backend design. Feature screens present public and authenticated workflows, Riverpod providers coordinate identity and asynchronous state, and typed Dart repositories perform Supabase operations. Server-side rules determine whether a caller may act on a patient record, care relationship, consultation, hospital, or notification. Client route guards improve navigation, while database authorization remains the enforcement boundary. [S2, S5]

blocks.p: Supabase Auth establishes the user session. PostgreSQL row-level security, function authorization, ownership predicates, and relationship grants constrain data operations. Private clinical files are accessed through authorized storage operations rather than public file URLs. Realtime subscriptions refresh allowed messages and notifications.

Transactional RPCs coordinate actions that update several records together. Booking, confirmation, rescheduling, and schedule changes use common locking rules so availability checks and reservation changes belong to the same operation. Edge Functions perform AI and notification work using server configuration.
Public client configuration contains the project URL, publishable key, and optional application URL. Privileged credentials, AI keys, SMTP passwords, and dispatcher tokens remain server-side.

blocks.p: The guest path verifies email before submitting intake and retains a reusable submission key. Approved guests activate their patient identity in place and continue tracking the authorized consultation. Registered patients submit online requests through the typed booking interface. Both paths require hospital confirmation before a new online reservation.

Information requests and schedule proposals give the patient a visible response action. Accepting an approved proposal rechecks availability and confirms atomically. Declining a proposal returns the request to hospital review. Face-to-face recommendations offer a new-booking action and do not create another reservation automatically.

The request status describes review and contact progress; the official consultation status describes the clinical appointment. Terminal operations synchronize the consultation, room, access grants, history, and notifications. [S5, S7]

CareNavigator PH uses a relational PostgreSQL database. The complete public-schema catalog contains 64 application tables and 906 columns, connected by 200 declared foreign-key constraints. The physical model also shows auth.users as an external platform identity reference. These counts come from the sanitized baseline catalog; the application schema is distinct from Supabase’s internal schemas. [S3, S11]

The complete physical ERD is presented through enlarged entity sheets and a foreign-key relationship register in Appendix D. Every application table and column is included. Tables with many columns continue onto another panel. A separate zoomable master diagram preserves all 200 relationship connectors in one view.

PK identifies a primary-key column. FK identifies a column that participates in a declared foreign key. UK marks membership in a unique key; columns of a composite key are unique as a tuple. The relationship register identifies the exact source and target columns, including composite references. Logical associations without a declared foreign key are not represented as database-enforced relationships.

An authentication user is distinct from an application users row. users.auth_user_id links those identities, while patient and doctor profiles refer to users.id. Relationship optionality comes from source-column nullability, and a maximum of one child is shown only when the foreign-key tuple has an unconditional uniqueness constraint.

Type labels are shortened for diagram readability: timestamptz means timestamp with time zone, timestamp means timestamp without time zone, and time means time without time zone. Numeric precision and scale are shown in the label, such as numeric_8_3_ for numeric(8,3). Array types use the suffix _array. User-defined type names remain unchanged.

blocks.p: The clinical output is the doctor's finalized structured checkup and its associated official records. A prescription issuance creates one order with its medication records, prescriber information, and signature validation. The notification output reports queued, sent, or failed according to the outbox state. Automatic summaries include only official prescriptions active on the summary date. Future and expired prescriptions are excluded. PRN directions remain directions and do not acquire invented administration times. Manual summary requests authorize that individual delivery.

blocks.p: CareNavigator PH implements a mobile and web application that connects public discovery, verified intake, hospital-reviewed booking, clinician documentation, patient records, communication, and administration. Flutter, Riverpod, and Supabase provide a shared technical foundation, while role and relationship checks define how each user participates in the care journey.

The repair work introduces typed booking outcomes, guest self-activation, reviewed patient uploads, atomic prescription orders, accurate delivery states, and a reproducible backend package. Recorded automated checks and release builds demonstrate progress. The project remains subject to the external integration and deployment acceptance gates identified in Chapter 4.

blocks.p: The master Mermaid source is generated from the table, column, primary-key, unique-key, and foreign-key metadata in supabase/baseline/catalog.json. Rendering uses the installed Mermaid Chart extension. The diagram source is docs/defense/full_database_erd.mmd; the vector master is docs/defense/full_database_erd.svg.

Each F-number in the master diagram identifies one foreign-key constraint in the relationship register. Source columns are listed before the arrow and referenced columns after it. “1 : 0..many” means each child requires one parent and a parent may have several children. “0..1 : 0..many” allows a child without a parent. “1 : 0..1” or “0..1 : 0..1” indicates that the source foreign-key tuple is also unique. Optional composite references are assessed from source nullability.

The auth.users reference belongs to the authentication platform and contributes one reference node, not an additional application table. Its referenced key is id (uuid). The 13 foreign keys that target auth.users are included in the 200-relationship total. No patient data or secret values appear in this appendix.

Conditional indexes and application checks can impose additional rules beyond the connectors shown here. Their full definitions remain in the baseline catalog and SQL. This ERD describes declared relationships and column structure; it does not replace row-level security policies or workflow authorization.
